pages.text: [#](53341a)Before a rite, you must prepare the ground. The circle is the structure that makes a working possible — a closed space where intention and power accumulate until released.[#]() [#](53341a)Right-click chalk on flat stone or earth to lay a glyph.[#]()
pages.title: Chalk

pages.text: [#](53341a)The ring is drawn in ordinary white chalk, but the single mark at the very centre must be drawn with **Golden Chalk**. That golden mark is the heart of the working: drop the ingredients beside it, then right-click the **golden** centre to begin.[#]()

[#](53341a)Mind this well, pupil — a white centre will not answer. Only the gold opens a rite. Many a circle has been drawn whole and true and still lay dead, because the witch forgot to gild its heart.[#]()
[#](53341a)Drawn from simple stuff. The stronger families are crafted or brewed from it.[#]()

[#](53341a)From ordinary chalk you may draw the stronger families: **Golden** with a gold nugget, yellow dye, and redstone; **Otherwhere** with artichoke, ender pearl, and lapis; **Infernal** with ember moss, blaze powder, and red dye.[#]()
pages.title: Stronger Chalks

pages.text: [#](53341a)Do not mistake their use. **Golden** is for no single rite — every working is begun from a golden centre, so keep some always at hand.[#]()

[#](53341a)It is the colour of the **ring** that must suit the rite: plain white for common workings, **Otherwhere** when the circle must reach across the boundary of worlds, **Infernal** for the things best not named lightly.[#]()
[#](53341a)Match the ring to the rite, and set gold at its heart.[#]()
